text: Long ago, the gods had grown weak, and they turned to Vishnu for help.
Go and churn the ocean of milk, he told them, and it will give you the nectar of immortality.
So they made a mountain their churning rod, and the serpent Vasuki their rope. Gods on one side, demons on the other, they pulled.
But the mountain began to sink.
So Vishnu became Kurma, a great tortoise, and carried the mountain on his back.
asr: So Vishnu became Kirma, a great tortoise, and carried the mountain on his back.

text: The ocean turned, and gave up its treasures.
A tree that grants every wish.
Then, standing on a lotus, came Lakshmi, the goddess of fortune. She looked at the gods and the demons, and she chose Vishnu.
Last of all rose the healer of the gods, holding a pot of amrita, the nectar.
This is the churning of the ocean: how the world was steadied, on the patient back of a tortoise.
